rows.evidence: Q1: Material and Methods and Results <U+2014> the authors report their own online questionnaire sent to 457 Bahia coffee growers in 2021, with 34 responses (7.4% return), and report frequencies of answers (e.g. 59.3% high prospect of PA use, 67.6% do not use PA, 51.7% cite lack of training as obstacle).
rows.notes: The study is a perception survey on the prospects of precision agriculture adoption among Bahia coffee growers; it does not measure or test remote sensing, geostatistics or spatial variability mapping, nor any effect on soil health or soil management. The only own result touching soil is that 62.1% of respondents thought PA is most important for soil management (a perception, not an outcome). All statements about geostatistics improving soil/nutrient management (Ferraz et al. 2015/2017, Figueiredo et al. 2018, Zanella et al. 2020, Jorge et al. 2019, Silva et al. 2020) are cited from other work in the Discussion and do not count. The study therefore provides no own evidence on remote sensing delivering soil health or effective soil management.

notes: Full text appears complete. Study is a small (n=34) descriptive grower perception survey on precision agriculture in general; it contains no field, remote sensing or soil data of its own.
